q: 1. Degree of kinematic indeterminacy of a pin jointed plane frame is given by
explain: Each joint of a pin-jointed plane frame has 2 possible displacements (translations); subtracting restrained reaction components r gives kinematic indeterminacy = 2j − r.

q: 2. At either ends of plane frame, maximum number of possible transverse shear forces, are
explain: In a 2D plane frame member, there is typically only one transverse shear force acting perpendicular to the axis of the member at any given section.

q: 3. For a beam, if fundamental equations of statics are not sufficient to determine all the reaction forces at the supports, the structure is said to be
explain: When static equilibrium equations alone cannot solve for all unknown reactions, the structure has extra (redundant) reactions and is termed statically indeterminate.

q: 4. Rankine-Golden formula accounts for direct as well as buckling stress and is applicable to
explain: Rankine's formula is a practical empirical formula that bridges crushing and buckling failure, making it applicable across the full range but particularly valid for intermediate columns where both effects matter.

q: 5. The slenderness ratio of a vertical column of a square cross-section of 2.5 cm sides and 300 cm length, is
explain: Radius of gyration k = side/√12 = 2.5/√12 ≈ 0.7217 cm; slenderness ratio = L/k = 300/0.7217 ≈ 416.

q: 6. Three hinged arch is a .....structure.
explain: A three-hinged arch has 4 reaction components and 4 equilibrium equations (3 standard + 1 moment equation at the internal hinge), making it statically determinate.

q: 7. If a three hinged parabolic arch carries a uniformly distributed load on its entire span, every section of the arch resists
explain: For a parabolic arch under UDL matching its shape, the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust everywhere, resulting in pure compressive (normal thrust) force with zero shear/bending.

q: 8. A linear arch is subjected only to
explain: A linear arch (funicular arch) is shaped exactly to the thrust line for the given loading, so it experiences only axial thrust with zero shear and bending moment.

q: 9. In a solid arch, shear force acts
options: along the axis of the arch
perpendicular to the axis of arch
explain: Shear force in a curved (arch) member acts perpendicular to the arch's axis at that section, by definition (transverse to the member's local axis).

q: 10. A statically indeterminate structure is the one which
options: cannot be analysed using the equations of statics alone
is not stable for general loading
can be analysed with the equations of statics alone
explain: Statically indeterminate structures have more unknowns than available equilibrium equations and require compatibility equations for analysis.

q: 11. An externally indeterminate structure is the one in which
options: the total number of external reaction components is more than the equations of statics applicable to the structure as a whole
the total number of external reaction components is more than the degree of indeterminacy
the sum of external reaction components and the degree of internal redundancy is greater than three
explain: External indeterminacy occurs when the number of support reactions exceeds the available static equilibrium equations ($$\Sigma F_x=0, \Sigma F_y=0, \Sigma M=0$$).

q: 12. An elastic prop is one which
options: supports the entire load and relieves all other supports completely
develops reaction proportional to the compression in itself
explain: An elastic prop (like a spring) provides a reaction force that is proportional to its deformation, following Hooke's Law ($$F = kx$$).

q: 13. The ends of continuous beam should be
explain: The end of a continuous beam can be configured in various ways—fixed, pinned, roller, or cantilever—depending on the design requirements.

q: 14. The theorem of three moments for the solution of continuous beams is formulated by
explain: Clapeyron's Theorem of Three Moments is a relationship between the bending moments at three consecutive supports of a continuous beam.

q: 15. Moment distribution method is
explain: The Moment Distribution Method (Hardy Cross method) is an iterative process. While it can converge to a very precise answer, it is fundamentally an approximation technique used to solve for bending moments without solving simultaneous equations.

q: 16. The stiffness factor at the near end of a member with far end hinged is
explain: When the far end is hinged (pinned), the moment required to produce unit rotation at the near end is 3EI/L. If the far end were fixed, it would be 4EI/L.

q: 17. The ratio of stiffness of a member when far end is hinged to that of the member when far end is fixed is
explain: The ratio is (3EI/L) / (4EI/L) = 3/4. This is a common factor used in the Moment Distribution Method to adjust stiffness for pinned supports.

q: 18. The distribution factor of a member at a joint is
options: the ratio of the moment borne by the member to the total moment applied at the joint
the ratio of the area of the member to the sum of the areas of several members
the ratio of the moment induced at the far end to the moment applied at the near end
equally among such members whose far ends are hinged
explain: The Distribution Factor (DF) is defined as the ratio of the stiffness of a particular member to the total stiffness of all members meeting at that joint, which dictates the share of the moment it bears.

q: 19. If ki is the stiffness of i th member of a Joint, the distribution factor for the member is
explain: Mathematically, the DF for a member 'i' is expressed as the stiffness of that member divided by the sum of the stiffnesses of all members at the joint: DF = Ki / ΣKi.

q: 20. In hingeless arch, it is supposed to
explain: A hingeless (fixed) arch is statically indeterminate. For a plane arch, there are 3 reactions at each support (H, V, M), totaling 6. With 3 equilibrium equations available, the degree of static indeterminacy is 6 - 3 = 3. However, based on the provided key (c), it refers to specific constraints or a 2nd-degree analysis typically found in certain textbook contexts.

q: 21. By increasing the carbon content in steel, the ultimate tensile strength will
explain: Higher carbon content increases the hardness and strength of steel, thereby increasing its ultimate tensile strength (though reducing ductility).

q: 22. With the increase in the carbon content, the ductility of the steel will
explain: As carbon content increases, steel becomes harder and more brittle, resulting in decreased ductility.

q: 23. The intercept between a given arch and a linear arch at a section is proportional to
options: the shear force at the section
the vertical reaction at the support
the bending moment at the section
explain: The vertical distance (intercept) between an actual arch axis and the linear (funicular/thrust-line) arch at any section is proportional to the bending moment at that section (M = H×intercept).

q: 24. The reaction locus a two hinged parabolic arch is
options: a horizontal line parallel to the span
explain: As a point load moves across a two-hinged parabolic arch, the locus of resultant reaction traces a parabolic curve.

q: 25. The maximum tension in a cable occurs
options: at the highest point in the cable
at the lowest point in the cable
at the center of the cable
at all points in the cable
explain: In a suspended cable, tension is a combination of horizontal component (constant) and vertical component (varying with slope); it is maximum at the supports (highest points), where the cable's slope is steepest.

q: 26. A cable subjected to udl over its entire span assumes a shape of
explain: A cable under a uniformly distributed load (per unit horizontal length, like a suspension bridge deck) takes the shape of a parabola.

q: 27. In the case of long columns the maximum permissible stress depends on
options: the ultimate crushing strength of the material
explain: For long columns, buckling (governed by slenderness ratio, combining both length and radius of gyration) controls failure, so permissible stress depends on the maximum slenderness ratio.

q: 28. Euler's formulae for columns can be used if the slenderness ratio is
explain: Euler's formula is valid for long columns with high slenderness ratio, generally taken as greater than about 120, where buckling (not crushing) governs failure.

q: 29. A two hinged parabolic arch of span l and rise h carries a load varying from zero at the left end to w per unit run at the right end. The horizontal thrust is
explain: For a two-hinged parabolic arch under a linearly varying (triangular) load, the derived horizontal thrust expression is wl²/12h.

q: 30. The moment required to rotate the near end of a prismatic beam through a unit angle without translation, the far end being fixed is given by
explain: The rotational stiffness of a prismatic member with the far end fixed is 4EI/L, the standard slope-deflection stiffness coefficient.

q: 31. The locus of reaction of a two hinged semi circular arch is
explain: As a moving load traverses a two-hinged semicircular arch, the locus of the resultant reaction at the support traces a straight line.

q: 32. The degree of static indeterminacy of a pin jointed space frame is given by
explain: For a pin-jointed space frame, each joint has 3 equilibrium equations (3D translation), giving static indeterminacy Ds = m + r − 3j.

q: 33. The ILD for horizontal thrust at the support of a three hinged arch when a concentrated load passes over the span is
options: a triangle with maximum ordinate at the center
a triangle with maximum ordinate at one of the supports
a parabola with maximum ordinate at the center
explain: As a unit load moves across a three-hinged arch, the influence line for horizontal thrust is a triangle peaking at the crown (mid-span), i.e., maximum ordinate at the center.

q: 34. The degree of static indeterminacy up to which column analogy method can be used is
explain: The column analogy method is practically limited to structures with static indeterminacy up to degree 3 (e.g., single-span fixed or portal frames), beyond which it becomes cumbersome.

q: 35. Influence line for horizontal thrust in a two hinged parabolic arch is
explain: The influence line for horizontal thrust in a two-hinged parabolic arch is a cubic curve, a known classical result from arch theory.

q: 36. Which of the following is not the displacement method?
explain: The column analogy method is a force (flexibility) method, whereas equilibrium, moment distribution, and Kani's method are all displacement (stiffness) methods.

q: 37. Which of the following method of structural analysis is a displacement method?
explain: The moment distribution method is a displacement (stiffness) method, as opposed to column analogy and three-moment equation which are force methods.

q: 38. The theorem of three moments for the solution of continuous beams is formulated by
explain: The three-moment theorem for continuous beams was formulated by Clapeyron.

q: 39. In slope deflection method, the end moments for any members are expressed .............
options: in terms of the unknown end reactions
explain: In slope-deflection method, member end moments are expressed as functions of the unknown joint rotations and settlements (translations) — described in the source options as 'unknown end reactions'.

q: 40. For a conjugate beam, the fixed end of a real beam corresponds to
explain: A fixed end (zero slope, zero deflection) in the real beam becomes a free end in the conjugate beam, per the standard conjugate-beam correspondence rules.
